name: JS-modules
origin: Extracted from Apple Press, https://github.com/lfcfoundry/apple-press (play: https://lfcfoundry.github.io/apple-press/), and Fancy, the Banana, https://github.com/lfcfoundry/fancy-banana (play: https://lfcfoundry.github.io/fancy-banana/)

modules.summary: Velvet stage curtains that slide shut over a page, then fly open; the velvet is painted by a small WebAssembly loop with plain JavaScript as the fallback.
modules.short: Velvet stage curtains that slide shut over a page and fly open.

modules.summary: Safe localStorage saves, backup slot, checksummed copy-paste save codes with a size limit on what a paste may unpack to.
modules.short: Safe saves in localStorage: backup slot, checksums, copy-paste save codes.

modules.summary: Hold-to-repeat for buttons that survives Android Chrome pointercancel.
modules.short: Hold-to-repeat buttons that survive Android Chrome's pointercancel.

modules.summary: Detects privacy modes that round timers (including Firefox's 16.67 ms clock), scramble canvas read-back or block storage, and says what it found in plain words.
modules.short: Detects privacy modes that blur timers, scramble canvas reads or block storage.

modules.summary: Steps visual effects down when the device cannot keep up; never back up behind the player.
modules.short: Steps visual effects down when the device cannot keep up; never back up mid-play.

modules.summary: Blurs a picture (a canvas, an ImageBitmap or RGBA bytes) on the graphics card with WebGL 2, or in WebAssembly, or in plain JavaScript, whichever the device does best; every way gives the same picture, and a big blur never freezes the page.
modules.short: Blurs a picture on the card (WebGL 2), in WebAssembly or plain JavaScript; same picture every way.

modules.summary: A big element scrolls away and a copy flies to its sticky mini version (and back).
modules.short: A big element scrolls away and a copy flies to its sticky mini version.

modules.summary: Die-cut sticker lettering in plain CSS text-shadow rings, no images.
modules.short: Die-cut sticker lettering in plain CSS, no images.

modules.summary: Tested maths for idle/clicker games: costs, buy-many and buy-max, milestones, away income, boost queue, number format.
modules.short: Tested maths for idle and clicker games: costs, buy-max, away income, number format.

modules.summary: Frame pacing for canvas games: even-dt smooths the frame time, quality-governor steps effects down and back up, job-pump spreads heavy jobs across frames, frame-meter shows frames a second, hitches and tap delay in plain words.
modules.short: Frame pacing for canvas games: smooth frame time, effect governor, job pump, frame meter.

modules.summary: Two hidden buttons for a game or app: five taps in a corner open a panel that saves a speed report (start-up, frames a second, slowest frames, heavy tasks, plain verdict) and an error log, as small Markdown files. No network.
modules.short: Hidden buttons that save a speed report and an error log from a real device. No network.

modules.summary: Tiny software 3D rasterizer that bakes shaded sprites to canvases once at load, or one frame per tick; also makes silhouette masks and packs sprite sheets. Optional WebAssembly fill add-on (same pixels, about 1.1 to 1.4 times faster baking in Chromium and Firefox).
modules.short: Tiny software 3D rasterizer that bakes shaded sprites to canvases.

modules.summary: Gamepad API to DOM focus: move through buttons, menus, sliders and drop-downs with a controller, no game code.
modules.short: Gamepad to focus: move through buttons, menus and sliders with a controller.

modules.summary: Loads PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF pictures so the page does not freeze when they are first drawn: picks the right off-thread way for each browser, loads a list in order, and tells whether the browser can read WebP or AVIF.
modules.short: Loads pictures with no freeze at first draw, the right way per browser, plus WebP/AVIF checks.

modules.summary: Keeps one open copy of a page in charge (Web Locks), so two tabs do not overwrite each other's saved data, and tells the game when the other copy closes.
modules.short: Keeps one tab in charge so two tabs never overwrite each other's saves.

modules.summary: Keeps the screen awake only while a game wants it: released on pause, hidden tab and idle, asked again when allowed, no retry storms.
modules.short: Keeps the screen awake only while a game wants it.

modules.summary: Makes the phone back swipe or back button close the top panel instead of leaving the page (CloseWatcher, with an opt-in history fallback for browsers without it).
modules.short: Makes the phone's back swipe close the top panel instead of leaving the page.

modules.summary: LZMA1 decoder that uses WebAssembly first (about 1.5 to 2.6 times faster to open a page) and falls back to a small readable ES5 JavaScript decoder; tested against Python's lzma. Browsers can only unpack gzip and deflate natively.
modules.short: LZMA decoder: WebAssembly first, small readable JavaScript fallback; tested against Python's lzma.

modules.summary: A PPMd (7-Zip PPMd7) decoder that uses WebAssembly first (about 1.4 to 1.8 times faster to open a page) and falls back to one ES5 JavaScript function, about 6.6 KB packed. It unpacks web-page data about 10% smaller than LZMA, but slower. PPMd is by Dmitry Shkarin; the public-domain code it follows is Igor Pavlov's, from 7-Zip.
modules.short: A PPMd (7-Zip PPMd7) decoder: WebAssembly first, JavaScript fallback; smaller than LZMA.

modules.summary: A written style guide plus demo for the soft, glossy cartoon 3D look done in plain CSS and SVG.
modules.short: A written style guide and demo for the soft, glossy cartoon 3D look in CSS and SVG.

modules.summary: Writes animated GIFs from canvas pictures with one shared palette, storing only the pixels that changed (about 6.8 times smaller than gifenc on a mostly still animation).
modules.short: Writes animated GIFs from canvas frames with one shared palette.

modules.summary: Turns pictures into a short MP4 or WebM video in the browser with the browser's own video encoder and two small file writers, no libraries; the same add/finish shape as gif-writer, and about 8 times smaller than a GIF of the same pictures in Netflow Map.
modules.short: Turns pictures into an MP4 or WebM video file.
modules.dependencies: none (needs the browser's WebCodecs video encoder)
modules.formats: browser global, CommonJS (module.exports; the file writers work in Node)

modules.summary: Opens .zip and Excel .xlsx files safely: limits counted on what really unpacks, so a zip bomb stops at the limit with a plain-words note.
modules.short: Opens .zip and .xlsx files safely, with limits counted on what really unpacks.

modules.summary: Keeps big data packed in memory and brings it back exactly, in one file with one pack/unpack: bytes and typed arrays (a 120 MB scene shrinks to 52%, 41% in small mode, and restores in about 239 ms in Firefox 158.0, against 312 ms with lz4-wasm and 1.5 s with fflate; lower is better) and big lists of plain JavaScript objects (300,000 link objects shrink to 14% of their JSON text, 35% for msgpackr with records). Picks the right layer by itself; MemoryCompressionJSO stays as an alias.
modules.short: Keeps big arrays, bytes and lists of objects packed in memory and brings them back exactly.

modules.summary: Keeps sorted whole numbers (ids, positions, links of every item of a map) in a third to a half of the memory of plain arrays and still answers 'value number i' and 'first value at or above x' without unpacking; also keeps many sorted lists in one structure and decodes them all at once. WebAssembly with SIMD, plain JavaScript fallback with the same answers.
modules.short: Packs sorted number lists small and searches them without unpacking.

modules.summary: Breadth-first distances and depth-first loop marking over a links-of-every-item layout in typed arrays, with no recursion. Same answers as Netflow Map's inline walks.
modules.short: Breadth-first distances and loop marking for link lists, in typed arrays.

modules.summary: Packs newline-delimited JSON (logs, events, API dumps) into LFC-pack (.json.lfc): every field becomes a typed column inside zstd blocks, with a footer of per-block number ranges. Reads back the same rows as JSON.parse (or the exact original bytes), only some keys, or only a time range, with helper workers for big files. WebAssembly is required; a Python reader is included.
modules.short: Packs NDJSON into small column files and reads the rows back, exactly if you ask.

modules.summary: Reads CSV or TSV text into typed columns: plain decimal columns come out as Float64Array straight from the bytes, the rest as text. The field scan runs in WebAssembly SIMD; plain JavaScript gives the same answers.
modules.short: Reads CSV and TSV into number and text columns, 3 to 11 times faster than common parsers.

modules.summary: Pcodec for web pages: unpacks (and optionally packs) big lists of numbers in a browser, one file, same bytes as any other Pcodec. The unpack-only file is 61 KB gzipped (the other JavaScript build of Pcodec is 324 KB), streams a 4,000,000-number file in 6.3 MB of memory, and WebAssembly is required (no plain-JavaScript backup).
modules.short: Pcodec number compression for web pages: unpack, and optionally pack, big lists of numbers.

modules.summary: Lays out a flow chart (Sankey) from a plain list of links, with about half the weighted crossings of d3-sankey on the charts measured, backward links drawn instead of crashing, and an SVG drawer.
modules.short: Lays out a Sankey flow chart from a list of links, with an SVG drawer.

modules.summary: The engine of Netflow Map as a module you can copy and adapt: nine views of a map and eleven network layouts, no two items on top of each other, WebAssembly twins for Force and Distances, and a use() hand-over for the layers and Sankey add-ons; a 30,000-item network lays out in about 0.8 s in the Netflow Map app (Firefox).
modules.short: Netflow Map's engine as an adaptable module: nine views, network layouts, add-on hand-over.
modules.dependencies: none to run; netflow-layers 1.2.0 or newer for the story views

modules.summary: Lays out a graph in rows (top to bottom or left to right) with story order, tags instead of very long links, a column for the pages every route passes, and tall maps cut into columns.
modules.short: Lays out a graph in rows, with tags for long links and tall maps cut into columns.

modules.summary: Turns a Netflow Map layout into plain drawing lists (dots, links, labels, ribbons, shapes) that Canvas 2D, WebGL2, WebGPU or SVG can draw the same way; big flat maps keep links in typed lists and reuse link looks between pictures.
modules.short: Turns a laid-out map into plain drawing lists for Canvas, WebGL or SVG.
modules.dependencies: none (uses netflow-engine output; netflow-engine's number formatter when present; the optional position index file needs elias-fano)

modules.summary: Simulates random walkers on a network with seeded, repeatable runs, 16 random-number distributions, 95% ranges and the exact odds to check against (1,000,000 walkers in about 52 ms with the WebAssembly loop in Chromium 155 and Firefox 158, lower is better). Big runs use a WebAssembly loop first, JavaScript when it cannot.
modules.short: Simulates random walkers on a network: seeded runs, 95% ranges, exact odds.

modules.summary: Keeps a short note, only on the device, of the errors, slow taps and long frames a page had; copyable as plain text, nothing is sent anywhere.
modules.short: A short private note of errors, slow taps and long frames, copyable as text.

modules.summary: A hold-then-drag task a young child will not finish, in front of the buttons and links a grown-up should press (a speed bump, not security).
modules.short: A hold-and-drag task a young child will not finish, in front of grown-up buttons.

modules.summary: A first-time tour: one dimmed layer, a bright window over the current part, Skip and Back, remembers who saw it and gives a finishing gift once.
modules.short: A first-visit tour: dimmed page, bright window, Skip and Back, remembers who saw it.

tools.summary: Font subsetting, safe inline-SVG tightening and a Zopfli self-extracting packer for one-file games.
tools.short: Font subsetting, safe inline-SVG tightening and a Zopfli self-extracting packer.

tools.summary: Packs one HTML file into a smaller self-unpacking file with LZMA and a hash check (Python 3 standard library).
tools.short: Packs one HTML file into a smaller self-unpacking file with LZMA (Python 3).

tools.summary: Packs one HTML file into a self-unpacking file with PPMd, the 7-Zip text compressor (PPMd by Dmitry Shkarin; public-domain code by Igor Pavlov, 7-Zip). Pure Python; pays off above about 60 KB of compressed data.
tools.short: Packs one HTML file into a self-unpacking file with PPMd (pure Python).

tools.summary: Seeded, reproducible random-input fuzzer engine with weighted operations, invariants, liveness checks and failure shrinking; Playwright and Puppeteer runners with real input and CPU throttling; stock-Firefox recipe; test-hook stripper.
tools.short: Seeded random-input fuzzer for games, with failure shrinking and browser runners.

tools.summary: Test-build counter for canvas 2D games: calls per frame, save/restore leaks, overhanging drawImage sources, draws below half size, style-write repeats, painted area.
tools.short: Test-build counter for canvas 2D games: calls per frame, leaks, repeated style writes.

tools.summary: Page that tells you in plain words whether copies of a page saved in different folders share their saved data, see each other's writes and locks; one button, copyable report.
tools.short: A one-button page that says whether copies of a page share their saved data.

tools.summary: Runs a Playwright-for-Python test in stock Firefox (through Selenium and geckodriver) without rewriting it; says plainly which calls it supports and stops with a clear message on the rest.
tools.short: Runs a Playwright-for-Python test in stock Firefox without rewriting it.

tools.summary: Drives WebKitGTK or GNOME Web from Node with no dependencies, using the call names of Playwright and Puppeteer (goto, evaluate, waitForFunction, mouse, keyboard, screenshot, console errors), so a test written for them can also run in WebKit.
tools.short: Drives WebKitGTK or GNOME Web from Node with Playwright-style calls, no dependencies.

tools.summary: Puts a prefix in front of every localStorage key on a test page, so a speed test or random-play run never touches the real saved game.
tools.short: Prefixes every localStorage key on a test page so tests never touch the real save.

tools.summary: One-button speed test run on the device: compares your page with parts switched off, keeps the scene in view and uncovered, and says the answer in plain sentences with a copyable table.
tools.short: A one-button speed test on the device: switches parts off and says what costs time.

tools.summary: Shared pieces for browser checks and speed tests: warm browsers, a four-browser runner, fair timing, skip-unchanged wasm builds, a wasm-versus-JavaScript twin test, a picture fingerprint gate and an automatic bisect.
tools.short: Warm browsers, fair timing, skipped rebuilds, wasm-vs-JS twin test, picture gate and bisect.

tools.summary: One command that says whether a release got slower than the one before it, from the speed-history files, and which browser checks a change needs re-run. It runs nothing itself, so it costs no browser time.
tools.short: Flags speed-history steps over 5% slower than the last release; lists the browser checks to re-run.

related.note: Story packages live with the editor they are generated from.

packages.summary: Create, clean, search, import and export interactive stories as JSON, with a JSON Schema. Twine import lives in twine-import.
packages.short: Create, clean, search, import and export interactive stories as JSON, with a schema.

packages.summary: Reads Twine stories (Twine 2 HTML, Twee 3, Twine 1) and turns SugarCube and Harlowe code into rules, with a plain-words report.
packages.short: Reads Twine stories (Twine 2 HTML, Twee 3, Twine 1) and turns their code into rules.

packages.summary: Turns an indented outline into pages and choices, or into a whole branching story.
packages.short: Turns an indented outline into pages and choices, or a whole branching story.

packages.summary: Says in plain words what one edit did to a story, such as "Add page “The Cellar”".
packages.short: Says in plain words what one edit did to a story.

packages.summary: Exact checker for branching stories with items, numbers and dice: dead ends and endings no player can reach.
packages.short: Exact checker for branching stories: dead ends and endings no player can reach.

packages.summary: Build one offline HTML game from a story, or play a story from code or a terminal.
packages.short: Builds one offline HTML game from a story, or plays a story from code or a terminal.

packages.summary: Layered, arc and matrix drawings of a story graph (SVG) and seeded simulated players.
packages.short: Layered, arc and matrix drawings of a story graph, plus simulated players.

packages.summary: Wrap a finished HTML page into a smaller page that unzips itself, with a pure-JS inflater fallback.
packages.short: Shrinks a finished HTML page into a self-unzipping page.

packages.summary: Tiered test runner and a Playwright-style API over WebDriver BiDi for stock Firefox; seeded random-story generator.
packages.short: Tiered test runner and Playwright-style API for stock Firefox, plus a random-story generator.

packages.summary: A guide and a helper (about 7.2 KB minified) for keeping two implementations of one rule set from drifting apart: seeded random inputs, a side-by-side comparison (also for async functions), shrinking a failing input to a small one, a field table and a time limit; runs in browsers too.
packages.short: Keeps two implementations of one rule set in step: random inputs, side-by-side comparison.

packages.summary: A written process and templates for a person and an AI assistant building software together.
packages.short: A written process and templates for a person and an AI assistant building software together.

groups.title: Device and browser adaptation
groups.use: Make a game behave on slow phones, privacy-focused browsers and power-saving screens.

groups.title: Saving and data safety
groups.use: Keep a player's progress safe and let them move it between devices.

groups.title: Games - Looks and effects
groups.use: Curtains, flying elements, lettering and 3D-looking sprites.

groups.title: Games - Controls
groups.use: Let players hold a button, or play with a gamepad.

groups.title: Games - Assist
groups.use: Show a new player around, and keep small children away from the buttons that matter.

groups.title: Games - Math
groups.use: The numbers behind idle and clicker games.

groups.title: Games - Testing
groups.use: Test a game by playing it at random, shrinking any failure to a short replay, counting what it draws and driving real browsers.

groups.title: App - Efficiency
groups.use: Keep a one-file app small and light: smaller data in memory, smaller pages on the wire.

groups.title: Model simulation
groups.use: Simulate random walkers over a graph.

groups.title: Visualization
groups.use: Draw maps, flow charts and animated pictures from data.

groups.title: Size and packaging
groups.use: Open zip and Excel files safely, and pack a finished page into a smaller file that unpacks itself.

groups.title: Story data
groups.use: Create, clean, import and save stories in one shared file format.

groups.title: Story validation
groups.use: Find dead ends and endings nobody can reach before a reader does.

groups.title: Story flow
groups.use: See a story's shape: maps of its pages and simulated readers.

groups.title: Story build and distribute
groups.use: Turn a story into a game, or play it from code or a terminal.

groups.title: Story packaging
groups.use: Pack a finished story page into a smaller page.

groups.title: Story testing
groups.use: Run tests on stock Firefox, generate random stories and keep two implementations in step.

groups.title: Working with an AI helper
groups.use: A written process for a person and an AI assistant building software together.
